title: Support and awards for elite athletes and SEA Games medallists
asked: Three MPs asked about reviewing Sports Excellence awards and support for elite athletes' training, welfare and long-term development; whether the Major Games Award Programme should recognise SEA Games silver and bronze medallists or use non-monetary recognition; and the breakdown of SEA Games 2025 funding by sport compared with the past five years.
asked_by: Ms Valerie Lee, Mr Alex Yam and Ms Elysa Chen
response: Mr David Neo said the Government invests in a High Performance Sport system, with spex programmes now supporting more than 1,500 carded athletes across 55 sports, up from 272 athletes across 14 sports in 1993. He cited spexPotential launched in 2024, spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarships, CPF top-ups for spexScholars, and a new Team Singapore home at Kallang. On awards, he said the Major Games Award Programme is a private SNOC-managed scheme funded by sponsors, and that SNOC has recently concluded its review and should announce updated awards in due course. He also pointed to feedback channels including coaches, NSAs and the Athletes Commission, and said last SEA Games spex recipients won half of medals and almost nine in 10 golds.

key_points.point: Government invests in a High Performance Sport system to nurture athletes to their fullest potential
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: The Government invests in a few areas to build up a strong High Performance Sport (HPS) system to nurture all our athletes to achieve their fullest sporting potential.

key_points.point: spex programmes now support more than 1,500 carded athletes across 55 sports, compared with 272 athletes across 14 sports in 1993
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: Today, we support more than 1,500 carded athletes across 55 sports, compared to 272 athletes across 14 sports when we first started spex in 1993.

key_points.point: spexPotential programme introduced in 2024 for younger athletes transitioning to higher levels
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: we introduced the spexPotential programme in 2024 to enhance support for younger athletes making the transition to higher levels of sporting success.

key_points.point: Inaugural spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarships awarded last year
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: Last year, we awarded our inaugural batch of spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarships.

key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: We also introduced Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-ups for spexScholars

key_points.point: New home of Team Singapore at Kallang will integrate the HPS ecosystem under one roof
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: the new home of Team Singapore, which will bring together the Singapore Sports School (SSP) to Kallang and integrate all elements of the HPS ecosystem under one roof

key_points.point: Major Games Award Programme is a private scheme managed by SNOC and funded by sponsors
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: It is a private award scheme that is managed by the Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC) and funded by their sponsors.

key_points.point: SNOC reviews the scheme periodically and decides award categories and monetary rewards in consultation with sponsors
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: SNOC reviews the scheme periodically and decides on the categories of awarded medallists and the monetary rewards offered to each of them, in consultation with sponsors.

key_points.point: Mr Yam's suggestion on SEA Games silver and bronze recognition will be requested for consideration in SNOC's review
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: We will take to heart Mr Yam's suggestion, and request for it to be considered in their review.

key_points.point: SNOC has recently concluded its review and should announce updated awards in due course
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: It is my understanding that SNOC has recently concluded the review. And I believe they should be ready to announce the updated Awards in due course.

key_points.point: At the last SEA Games, spex Scholars and spex Potential recipients won half of medals and almost nine out of 10 gold medals
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: our spex Scholars as well as our spex Potential recipients won half of our medals and almost nine out of 10 of every gold medal that was won

key_points.point: School Sports Fiesta announced last year to broaden sport access for children from all backgrounds
key_points.speaker: Mr David Neo
key_points.quote: last year we announced the School Sports Fiesta

left_open: The breakdown of funding allocated to national athletes competing in SEA Games 2025 across different sports
How funding levels compare to the past five years
Whether athletes are asked about satisfaction levels of spex
Plans to expand the SportCares Bursary specifically
Adjustments planned to better support athletes' competitive readiness for future regional tournaments
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered athlete welfare assessment, feedback channels, SEA Games award review timeline, funding effectiveness, and sport access for lower-income youth.
